goal: Watch the support (opponent) arm place five objects into the far basket one after another, then place your five matching objects into your basket in that same order, and finish with both arms back at their start pose.
instruction_templates: Observe the object placement order, remember it, then place the corresponding objects into the basket in the same order.
success: Five stages, evaluated strictly in order (stage k+1 is only tested after stage k has been passed). Let target_label[0..4] be the five agent-side objects (labels t0..t4 in some permutation) listed in the order the support arm placed their copies aim_i (the permutation is stored in a per-seed trajectory pickle; not known statically).

Stage k (k = 0..4), true at one action boundary: target_label[i] is in basket0 for every i <= k, AND target_label[i] is NOT in basket0 for every i > k, AND all five demonstrator objects aim0..aim4 are in basket1.
'In basket' = object origin xy inside the convex hull of the basket's world bbox and object origin z above the basket bbox z_min (is_A_in_B / is_A_not_in_B).
Stage 4 (the last) additionally requires all_robot_back_to_origin(): each target arm within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of its start pose.
Additionally two 'query' rules must never be violated (see evaluation).
evaluation: Stages are held in a queue: after every action only the first not-yet-passed stage is tested; when it holds it is removed (at most one stage per action). Success when all 5 are removed. Because stage k demands that later objects are not in basket0, the objects must enter basket0 one at a time in exactly the demonstrated order. Two failure queries are counted every action and any count > 0 immediately fails the episode (reward 0, episode ends): (Q1) FAIL if at an action boundary [left_arm OR right_arm is 'not back to origin' (pos > 0.3 m on any axis or rot > 30 deg from start pose)] AND [support_arm0 is not back to origin (pos > 0.3 m on any axis or rot > 40 deg)]. I.e. the agent must not move its arms far away while the support arm is demonstrating. (Q2) FAIL if at an action boundary, for any k in {4,3,2,1}: [all target grippers open (>=0.8) AND target_label[k] has moved < 0.004 m since the previous evaluation of this check AND target_label[k] is in basket0 AND at least one of target_label[0..k-1] is NOT in basket0]. I.e. releasing an object in basket0 while an earlier-demonstrated object is still missing is an immediate failure (wrong order). Otherwise fails at step_lim.
objects: t0..t4: five agent-side objects, one from each of five categories (toy_car idx 0-4, action_camera, phone, watch idx 0-2, garage idx 14-15; categories sampled so each of the 5 categories appears once, one unique instance each), start in x in [-0.3,0.4], y in [-0.2,-0.05] (table frame), random yaw up to 180 deg; prohibited area x[-0.1,0.1], y[-0.2,-0.15]
aim0..aim4: demonstrator copies of t0..t4 (same model each: aim_i same_as t_i), start in x in [-0.3,0.25], y in [0.1,0.3] (table frame), random yaw
basket0: basket idx 5, static geometry, fixed at table (-0.4,-0.15), z 0.04 -- the agent's target basket
basket1: basket idx 5, fixed at table (0.35, 0.25), z 0.04 -- the demonstrator's basket
scene_dynamics: A second, non-target arm (support_arm0, a Franka in robot_config dual_x5_and_franka_competition) replays a pre-recorded joint trajectory that picks aim objects and puts them into basket1 in the secret order. The trajectory is queued after the agent's first action and is consumed in lock-step with the agent's actions (collect_interval control sub-steps per action), so it plays during the first part of the episode while the agent is also acting. After it finishes, the scene is validated once: if any aim_i is not in basket1 the sample is flagged unstable and dropped from the evaluation.
needs_memory_or_language: Yes: the agent must watch (via cameras) the order in which the support arm moves the five objects into basket1, remember it, and reproduce it with the matching (same-model) objects on its own side. The order is different per seed and nothing in the instruction states it.
end_requirements: Final stage: both target arms within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of their start pose (all_robot_back_to_origin, defaults). Grippers need not be open for success.
notes: The order is only known at runtime (labels are read from the pickle in Assets/Traj/<benchmark>/imitate_sorting_sequence/<eval_seed>/<seed>.pkl). Q2 as written: the nested lists inside the query are combined as OR over k=4..1 of AND(gripper open, not moved, in basket0, OR(earlier ones not in basket0)). Each is evaluated with short-circuiting; is_not_moved(update=True) compares against the position stored at its last evaluation (initially the episode-start pose). Q1 limits are loose (0.3 m per axis / 30 deg for the agent arms) so only large arm motions during the demonstration cause failure. Whether the agent may begin acting before the demonstration ends is allowed by the code but any large arm excursion during it is a failure. Predicate conventions (from func_parser.py): object 'position' = the object's root/origin position in world coordinates (metres, z up); 'bbox' = the 8 corners of the object's local bounding box transformed to world; is_A_in_B = A's origin xy lies inside the convex hull of B's world-projected bbox AND A's origin z > B's bbox z_min; is_axis_up(label, axis, threshold) = angle between (object rotation applied to the local axis) and world +z is < threshold degrees (wrapper default threshold 15 deg); is_axis_aligned = angle between two (optionally functional-point-frame) axes < align_threshold degrees, optionally after projection onto a plane (project_plane='xy' drops z and renormalises); all_robot_back_to_origin() default = for every target (agent-controlled) arm, end-effector pose vs its pose at episode start: |dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m (per-axis, not Euclidean) and orientation difference <= 20 deg; is_all_gripper_open(open_threshold) = every target gripper's normalised opening ((val-scale0)/(scale1-scale0)) >= open_threshold (wrapper default 0.6).
